ai_technology: Support-vector classification with an RBF kernel and logistic regression learn transit signatures from cell/nuclear contour trajectories; feature selection and Shapley analysis identify predictive shape descriptors.

evidence.ai_role: Support-vector classification with an RBF kernel and logistic regression learn transit signatures from cell/nuclear contour trajectories; feature selection and Shapley analysis identify predictive shape descriptors.
evidence.tested: Trajectory-level train/validation/test partitions, comparison with random-classifier baselines and transfer to narrower constrictions and adhesive surfaces.
evidence.unknown: One cell line; observational predictive associations, no causal perturbation establishing morphology as mechanism and no clinical metastasis validation.

organization: Laboratoire de Physique de l’École Normale Supérieure, ENS, Université PSL, CNRS, Sorbonne Université, Université Paris Cité; Laboratoire Jean Perrin, Sorbonne Université, CNRS

source_review.scope: Primary manuscript Methods, relevant Results, limitations and first-version publication metadata reviewed.

summary: Support-vector and logistic classifiers linked cell area and circularity to whether MDA-MB-231 breast-cancer cells would traverse microfluidic constrictions. Less circular cells were more likely to transit, and trajectory features about 30 minutes before an event were most informative. Models transferred without retraining to narrower constrictions and more adhesive surfaces. This preprint reports a condition-dependent association in one cell line, not a causal mechanism or a predictor of metastasis in patients.
title: Learned cell-shape signatures predict confined transit
